name: BPC-157
common_claim: heals tendon, ligament and gut injury
notes: Reference case for the hack: large preclinical literature, almost no human data, heavy single-group concentration

name: TB-500
notes: Marketed as a fragment of thymosin beta-4; check whether cited studies used the fragment or the full protein

name: Thymosin alpha-1
notes: Approved in some countries, not an approved US product; good test of regional status handling

name: GHK-Cu
notes: Widely used topically in cosmetics; injectable use is the gray-market part

name: Semax
notes: Most literature is Russian-language; a good stress test for non-English retrieval

name: Selank
notes: Same retrieval problem as Semax

name: Ipamorelin
common_claim: growth hormone release without appetite increase
notes: Was taken into industry development then dropped; find out why

name: CJC-1295
notes: Check whether cited data is for the DAC or non-DAC version - vendors conflate them

name: Sermorelin
notes: Was an approved US product and was withdrawn; withdrawal reason is the interesting part

name: Tesamorelin
common_claim: reduces visceral fat in HIV lipodystrophy
notes: Positive control: a real approval with real trials

name: AOD-9604
common_claim: fat loss without growth hormone effects
notes: Went through human obesity trials and did not meet endpoints; now sold as a supplement. Strong control: real human data with a negative result

name: Melanotan II
notes: Has published case reports of harm - use for the safety track

name: Bremelanotide
notes: Positive control, and the approved cousin of Melanotan II

name: Epitalon
notes: Khavinson bioregulator literature; near-total single-group concentration

name: MOTS-c
aliases: mitochondrial open reading frame of the 12S rRNA type-c
notes: Real academic literature, almost no human intervention data

name: DSIP
notes: 1970s-80s literature, little since; check publication dates

name: KPV
notes: Short tripeptide; literature is mostly cell and mouse models

name: LL-37
notes: Genuine research peptide with a large literature; useful as a 'lots of evidence but not a drug' control

name: Semaglutide
notes: Strongest positive control in the set. An agent that reports 'no good evidence' here is broken

name: Tirzepatide
notes: Second positive control

name: Retatrutide
notes: Investigational with published trial data; tests whether agents distinguish 'in trials' from 'approved'
